context.body: King David was told, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of God’s ark.” So David went and brought up God’s ark from….
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David brings the ark from Obed-Edom with sacrifice and shouting, blesses and distributes food, then meets Michal’s contempt and answers about his abasement.
observations.label: The ark enters Jerusalem with sacrifice and dancing: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, the ark bearers, Israel, Michal, and each household, Obed-Edom’s house, David’s city, the tent, and royal household, bringing, sacrificing, dancing, shouting, blessing, distributing, despising, and answering visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: The ark enters Jerusalem with sacrifice and dancing: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, the ark bearers, Israel, Michal, and each household · Obed-Edom’s house, David’s city, the tent, and royal household · bringing, sacrificing, dancing, shouting, blessing, distributing, despising, and answering · public celebration ends in household estrangement
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 6:12–23

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 6:12–23 as its own ark, house, and kingdom David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places public celebration ends in household estrangement inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
